newsitem.title: USA: Guidant gets FDA clearance for catheter.
newsitem.headline: Guidant gets FDA clearance for catheter.

text.p: Guidant Corp said Tuesday that the ACS Rx Comet, its newest rapid-exchange coronary dilatation catheter, has been cleared for marketing by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
Guidant said the catheter, manufactured by its Advanced Cardiovascular Systems Inc unit, is used to open blocked arteries during percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA).

Guidant said the ACS RX COMET catheter marks the group's second new product introduction this month and further expands the range of choices available to physicians when selecting angioplasty catheters.

"The ACS RX COMET catheter is yet another addition to our family of balloon catheter system sizes, including the 15-millimeter balloon," Ginger Howard, president of Guidant's Vascular Intervention group, said in a statement.

The ACS RX COMET catheter has been approved and available outside the United States since July 1996, and is part of Guidant's broad product portfolio. Marketing of this catheter in the United States will begin immediately.
